issue_context.title: Call `TaskController.Stop()` can't make producer exit in spmcpool
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
TestAddIndexUniqueFailOnDuplicate with TiDBEnableDistributeReorg(true) 

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
Executed successfully.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

We encountered an error and the consumer exits early by calling `TaskController.Stop()`, but the producer doesn't exit, so the test can't return normally.

```
goroutine 13890 [chan send, 9 minutes]:
github.com/pingcap/tidb/util/gpool/spmc.(*Pool[...]).AddProduceBySlice.func1()
	/Users/xia/workspace/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb/util/gpool/spmc/spmcpool.go:299 +0x2be
created by github.com/pingcap/tidb/util/gpool/spmc.(*Pool[...]).AddProduceBySlice
	/Users/xia/workspace/src/github.com/pingcap/tidb/util/gpool/spmc/spmcpool.go:277 +0x44d
```

It seems we need to notify the producer when `TaskController.Stop()`.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/40542

review_comments: Sorry, It is unnecessary to delete.
It is useless and lead to data race.

https://github.com/uber-go/guide/blob/master/style.md#channel-size-is-one-or-none

In my experience, it's really helpful to force us to think about more extreme situations and avoid bug in advance. I'm more like unbuffered channel now because we always need to deal with sender's blocking (golang has no unlimited length channel) and unbuffered channel means we do not need to drain elements when receiver is closing
Agree with you. Let me set TaskChanLen's default value as 1.

Why call `Done` here? I seem we call `Done` https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/41016/files#diff-526c36d8ad42670e920fd84ae336d6b60196c61639bfa1c3a572adad64d1836cR283.
Rest LGTM

This ```waitgroup``` is to wait for the producer and all tasks to be completed. But when we force the produce and all workers to stop, Some tasks are still in the queue. we need to mark this complete. then ```Wait``` can exit.
Could we add the `control.Stop()` here, like https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/40542/files#diff-192b5bb5d7cd86dfa5e5223cdece209444dc6b5de220d92648d4385098228b9bR183-R190
